Pakistan Prime Minister Faces Social Media Scrutiny Following Hong Kong Sixes Win

31 Oct 2026, 07:37 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: news.abplive.com

Image: Prateek Thakur · Photo source · Cropped to 16:9; original source image

Match Summary

In the opening round of the Hong Kong Sixes 2026, the Pakistan cricket team secured a four-wicket victory over India. India batted first, setting a target of 89 runs in their allotted six overs, bolstered by an explosive 40-run performance from Shashank Singh.

Pakistan successfully chased the target in just 3.5 overs. The innings was defined by aggressive batting, particularly from captain Abbas Afridi and Khawaja Nafay. Key aspects of the chase included:

  • Opening Assault: Abbas Afridi hit five consecutive sixes in the opening over.
  • Efficient Scoring: Pakistan reached the required 89 runs rapidly, with Nafay remaining unbeaten on 41 runs from 12 balls.
  • Bowling Efforts: Pakistan’s bowling lineup, led by Abdul Samad’s double-wicket over, managed to restrict India's scoring potential in the latter half of the first innings.

Official Response and Public Reaction

Following the result, Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif posted a message on social media platform X, congratulating the team for their performance and commending the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) leadership for their support.

However, the post generated significant backlash from online users. Criticism centered on two main themes:

  • Significance of the Tournament: Many users questioned the stature of the Hong Kong Sixes, an ICC-sanctioned, non-traditional format event, arguing that it does not carry the same weight as major international tournaments like the ICC World Cups or the Asia Cup.
  • Contextual Accuracy: Some commenters pointed out inaccuracies in the Prime Minister's post, specifically noting that the match was not Pakistan’s opening clash of the tournament, as the team had previously faced the UAE.

Understanding the Format

The Hong Kong Sixes is a shortened version of cricket organized by Cricket Hong Kong, China. It is distinct from the standard T20 or One Day International (ODI) formats used in primary global cricket competitions.

How to Verify Official Results

Readers interested in verifying match details or the official status of the tournament can visit the following resources:

  • Cricket Hong Kong, China: Official tournament portals and schedules.
  • International Cricket Council (ICC): Records regarding sanctioned events and tournament standings.
  • Public Statements: Official communications from the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) regarding their participation in current international fixtures.
